walkthrough.title: One chart, read in four steps
walkthrough.lead: The Life Palace first, then sanfang sizheng, then the Four Transformations, and the Decade last. That is the order Ni Haixia read a chart in.
walkthrough.note: Sample chart: a made-up birthday, worked out by the charting engine in your browser

ming.label: Step 1 · Life Palace
ming.title: Your character, at a glance
ming.body: The Life Palace is in Zi and holds Wuqu and Tianfu, with Wuqu taking Huaquan. You have strong views; managing money and making decisions are your strengths, and you do best when you call the shots.
ming.basis: Basis: the Life Palace’s main stars and Huaquan

sanfang.label: Step 2 · Sanfang sizheng
sanfang.title: Know where your effort goes
sanfang.body: The Office Palace holds Ziwei and Tianxiang: you suit a senior role in a large organization. The opposite Travel Palace holds Qisha: a lot of travel and change. The Wealth Palace holds Lianzhen: money comes from professional skill.
sanfang.basis: Basis: read the Life Palace together with the Wealth, Office and Travel palaces (paraphrased from Ni Haixia, Tian Ji lecture 2, part 1, 00:12:58)

sihua.label: Step 3 · Four Transformations
sihua.title: What flows, what sticks
sihua.body: Taiyang takes Hualu and Taiyin takes Huake in the Parents Palace: close ties with your elders, and a lot of help from your parents. Tiantong takes Huaji in the Brothers Palace: friction comes easily with siblings and friends.
sihua.basis: Basis: the birth-year Four Transformations (a Geng year: Taiyang Lu, Wuqu Quan, Taiyin Ke, Tiantong Ji)

daxian.label: Step 4 · Decade
daxian.title: Ten years at a time: which one is yours
daxian.body: You are {age} now, in the {start}–{end} Decade, in the Children Palace. It has no main star, so read it through the stars of the opposite Estate Palace, Tianji and Jumen: a decade with a lot going on at home, and a good chance of moving house.
daxian.basis: Basis: the Decade, and borrowing stars from the opposite palace

outlook.line1: The point of glimpsing your fate ahead of time
outlook.line2: is not to foresee the future
outlook.line3: but to keep coming to know yourself
outlook.closing: and, in the end, to write the story of your own life

features.title:
Ziwei Doushu
as Ni Haixia taught it
features.subtitle: Not a simplified version. It follows Ni Haixia’s teaching strictly.
points: Builds the chart from the Nayin Five Phases Configuration, not from the simplified formulas found online.
Places the Life Palace by counting the birth hour backward and the Body Palace by counting it forward, exactly as the lessons teach.
Works out the 14 Main Stars and the Four Transformations (sihua) by the original method, complete and easy to check.

features.title:
All 14 Main Stars.
Not one missing.
features.subtitle: Main Stars, Secondary Stars and the Four Transformations, all on one screen
points: Each of the 14 Main Stars in its palace, with how they relate in plain view
Secondary Stars and Baleful Stars on the same screen, nothing important left out
Brightness grades (Miao, Wang, Li, Xian) beside each star name, so strong and weak show at a glance
Click any Main Star to read Ni Haixia’s detailed explanation of it.

features.title:
Easy to read.
Easy to ask.
features.subtitle: A knowledge base of Ni Haixia’s method × Claude
points: Your character: read from the Main Stars of your Life Palace, together with its sanfang sizheng
Six topics, one tap apart: overview, personality, career, love, wealth and health
Decade and Year tracking: the focus of your current 10-year Decade, plus specific tips and next steps from this year’s Year palace.
Follow-ups: ask about anything you didn’t follow, like “My Life Palace has no main star. How do I read it?”

features.title:
Finds the geju
in your chart
features.subtitle: Geju are fixed combinations of stars, as the old books name them
points: Automatically detects 11 classic geju, such as Zifu tonggong (Ziwei and Tianfu sharing a palace), Shapolang, Jiyue tongliang, Lianzhen–Tianxiang and Wuqu–Qisha.
Precisely spots special geju such as Zuofu and Youbi flanking the Life Palace, or Taiyang and Taiyin (the Sun and the Moon) flanking it, and gives the standard reading from Ni Haixia’s method.
Automatically flags when the Four Transformations land in the Life Palace or the Travel Palace, and points out the life issues to watch.

Your Office Palace holds Tianliang, which the old books call the sheltering star. With Zuofu in its sanfang, you tend to find help when you take things on…
What does Huaji in the Marriage Palace mean?

ziwei.name: Ziwei
ziwei.heading: Ziwei
ziwei.brief: The noble star of heaven, leader of all the stars. People with Ziwei in the Life Palace have a proud, aloof air. It stands for authority and success, and for a born leader’s presence. They do best in leading roles where they take full charge.

tianji.name: Tianji
tianji.heading: Tianji
tianji.brief: A star of long life, standing for strategy and change. Bright and quick-witted, good at planning and attentive to detail. Suited to planning, consulting and technical work.

taiyang.name: Taiyang
taiyang.heading: Taiyang (the Sun)
taiyang.brief: The main star of the Office Palace, standing for reputation and fame. Generous and big-hearted, it cares about its public image and favors government and public service. It is stronger in a man’s chart, and at Miao brightness it is open and upright.

wuqu.name: Wuqu
wuqu.heading: Wuqu (Military Corner)
wuqu.brief: The main star of the Wealth Palace, standing for money and decisiveness. Strong-willed and bold in action, it suits finance, banking, the military and the police. A lonely star that clashes with others, so marrying later is better.

tiantong.name: Tiantong
tiantong.heading: Tiantong
tiantong.brief: The main star of the Fortune Palace, standing for enjoyment and getting along with people. Gentle and very well liked, it values a good quality of life and has tender feelings. Fortune is good in later years.

lianzhen.name: Lianzhen
lianzhen.heading: Lianzhen (Pure Virtue)
lianzhen.brief: A lesser romance star, standing for talent and desire. Highly gifted and full of feeling, it suits the arts and politics. Talented in many ways, but it should beware of romantic trouble.

tianfu.name: Tianfu
tianfu.heading: Tianfu
tianfu.brief: The lead star of the Southern Dipper, standing for the treasury and savings. Steady, careful and good with money, it is the stabilizing force in a chart. Suited to managing finances and administration.

taiyin.name: Taiyin
taiyin.heading: Taiyin (the Moon)
taiyin.brief: The main star of the Estate Palace, standing for wealth and a gentle, yin nature. Tender and sensitive, it is especially good in a woman’s chart. Good for property and savings, and suited to the arts or service work.

tanlang.name: Tanlang
tanlang.heading: Tanlang (Greedy Wolf)
tanlang.brief: The romance star, standing for desire and talent. Talented in many ways, with strong desires and an active social life. Suited to the arts, public relations and business, and very well liked.

jumen.name: Jumen
jumen.heading: Jumen (Huge Gate)
jumen.brief: The dark star, standing for speech and disputes. A gifted speaker and sharp thinker, it suits law, teaching and the media. Watch out for gossip and quarrels; it makes its way by the power of argument.

tianxiang.name: Tianxiang
tianxiang.heading: Tianxiang
tianxiang.brief: The seal star, standing for support and official authority. Good at bringing people together, polite, honest and law-abiding. Suited to advisory, administrative and legal work, and lucky in finding helpful patrons.

tianliang.name: Tianliang
tianliang.heading: Tianliang
tianliang.brief: The shelter star, standing for maturity and protection. Upright, steady and deeply kind, it is watched over by heaven. Suited to medicine, social work and religion.

qisha.name: Qisha
qisha.heading: Qisha
qisha.brief: The general star, standing for fierce strength and pioneering. Tough, quick to act and unafraid of challenges, it suits starting a business, the military and police, and competitive fields. It can turn bad luck into good.

pojun.name: Pojun
pojun.heading: Pojun (Destroyer of the Army)
pojun.brief: The spending star, standing for change and breaking new ground. Bold and unafraid of change, it brings a life of big changes but plenty of nerve. Suited to pioneering work, taking roads no one has walked before.

hualu.name: Hualu
hualu.heading: Hualu (Transformation of Luck)
hualu.brief: A star of blessing comes to the palace, bringing more wealth and good fortune. Things in that palace go smoothly and abilities grow. It is the most welcome transformation in a chart.

huaquan.name: Huaquan
huaquan.heading: Huaquan
huaquan.brief: A star of power comes to the palace, bringing control and leadership. In that palace it brings strength and decisiveness. It does best in the Office Palace and the Life Palace, where it means real power at work.

huake.name: Huake
huake.heading: Huake
huake.brief: A star of honors comes to the palace, bringing a good name and helpful patrons. In that palace it brings a name for learning and luck in exams, with support from others. Good for study, exams and public life.

huaji.name: Huaji
huaji.heading: Huaji (Transformation of Taboo)
huaji.brief: A star of trials comes to the palace, bringing fixations and obstacles. Watch that palace closely: the part of life it covers will become an important test.

trinity.title: Heaven · Earth · Humanity
trinity.intro:
A chart is not your whole life.

Ni Haixia divided what shapes a life into three parts: heaven, earth and people.

cards.label: Fate at birth
cards.desc: The moment you are born fixes where the stars fall, your Five Phases Configuration and the Main Stars of your Life Palace. That is the base of a life, and only a third of it.

cards.label: Where you live
cards.desc: The city and family you are born into, and the place you live, make up another third. The same chart can lead to very different lives in different places.

cards.label: Heart and mind
cards.desc: Your own will, attitude, choices and actions are the most active force for changing fate. Ni Haixia stressed that we learn our chart to become better people, not to sit and wait for fate to decide. The chart sets the base. What you make of it is yours.

trinity.quote: Ni Haixia held that a natal chart is only one third of a life; the other two are where you live and your own choices.

ni.title: Ni Haixia
ni.intro:
One of the most influential masters of Chinese medicine and the divination arts in the modern Chinese-speaking world

Founder of the Hantang College of Chinese Medicine in the US · His Ren Ji and Tian Ji teaching series live on

stats.label: Legacy
stats.sub: Classical formula medicine · Yijing (Book of Changes)

bio.life: : Ni Haixia (1954–2012) was born in Taiwan. As a young man he studied under several noted doctors of Chinese medicine and specialized in the Jingfang (classical formula) school, the tradition of the Shanghan lun (Treatise on Cold Damage). In midlife he moved to the United States to practice medicine and founded the Hantang College of Chinese Medicine, where for more than twenty years he taught Chinese medicine and the traditional divination arts in a systematic way. He died of liver cancer in Taiwan on January 31, 2012, at the age of 58.
bio.teaching: : Ni Haixia organized everything he had learned into two public teaching series. Ren Ji covers the Zhenjiu dacheng (Great Compendium of Acupuncture and Moxibustion), the Shennong bencao jing (Divine Farmer’s Classic of Materia Medica), the Huangdi neijing (Inner Classic of the Yellow Emperor), the Shanghan lun (Treatise on Cold Damage) and the Jingui yaolüe (Essentials from the Golden Cabinet). It is the “principles of humankind,” a complete path for learning Chinese medicine. Tian Ji covers Ziwei Doushu and the Yijing (Book of Changes). It is the “principles of heaven,” his systematic work on the divination arts. Together they are the most complete legacy Ni Haixia left to later generations.
bio.stance: : In Ziwei Doushu, Ni Haixia belonged to the Southern Sanhe (Three Harmonies) school. He read the Life Palace as the root and the sanfang sizheng as its use, and he used only the birth-year Four Transformations, not feihua (transformations flown from palace stems).
bio.approach: <label>Approach to learning</label>: Ni Haixia was against memorizing formulas by rote; he put understanding the principles and sound logic first. This attitude helped Ziwei Doushu move from secrets passed from master to student toward knowledge anyone can study systematically.
bio.influence: <label>Influence today</label>: Ni Haixia’s lecture videos are widely shared on Bilibili, YouTube and other major platforms, and a new generation of fate-reading and Chinese medicine fans sees them as required viewing for beginners. He was not only an heir to Ziwei Doushu but also one of the key figures who brought traditional fate reading and Chinese medicine into modern knowledge.

ni.disclaimer: All readings on this site draw on Ni Haixia’s public Tian Ji lecture notes, the Ming edition of the Ziwei doushu quanshu (Complete Book of Ziwei Doushu) and classic texts of the traditional Sanhe school. They are for cultural interest and personal growth only. Ni Haixia himself has no commercial connection with this site.

teachings.title:
The minggong is the root from whence we start;
The sanfang is the use that plays its part.
teachings.body: Ni Haixia always stressed that reading a chart starts with the Life Palace (minggong). Its Main Stars set a person’s basic pattern and inborn character, while the sanfang (the Wealth, Office and Travel palaces) decide where that person can put their strengths to use. Only the four palaces read together give the full picture of a life.

teachings.title: Never overlook stars borrowed from the opposite palace
teachings.body: What set Ni Haixia apart was the weight he gave to the opposite palace. When a palace is empty, with no Main Star, it must be read using the stars of the palace across from it. Across from the Life Palace is the Travel Palace, and the two shape each other. Many beginners miss this key point.

teachings.title: The Four Transformations mark what weighs most
teachings.body: Hualu, Huaquan, Huake and Huaji mark what weighs most in a chart. The same star reads differently with Hualu than with Huaji.

teachings.title: Each Decade lasts ten years, and fortune moves in stages
teachings.body: Ni Haixia divided life into 12 Decades of 10 years each. He held that a person’s fortunes are completely different from one Decade palace to the next. Only by knowing which Decade you are in now, and which stars sit in its palace, can you truly make the most of your fortune today.

heming.title: Ziwei Compatibility
heming.desc:
Enter two people’s birth details. Following Ni Haixia’s method, AI reads their Marriage Palaces side by side and looks at how their Life Palaces and sanfang sizheng fit together,

to see how the two of you get along and where you complement each other.

closing.title:
Twelve palaces.

One clear chart.
closing.desc:
Enter the date and hour of your birth, and all twelve palaces are laid out in seconds.

AI then reads them from the Life Palace out: character, career, love, wealth and health.
